text: For rumen microbes to grow well, multiply, and properly digest forage, the rumen needs the right temperature, pH, and nutrients — without these, microbes cannot convert straw into energy and protein. Growth requirements include: a cellulose source (forage, straw) or starch source (corn, cassava root) for energy; a nitrogen source (grass, foliage, or urea) to produce ammonia; minerals (phosphorus, calcium, magnesium); trace elements (copper, zinc, manganese, iron, sulfur); and vitamins A, D, E, supplied by good-quality forage or a premix — ruminants can themselves produce B-group vitamins.
